claims.text: Minor alloying additions create controlled compositional heterogeneities in CoCrFeNi.
The introduced compositional heterogeneities locally reduce the effective stacking-fault energy.
Reduced stacking-fault energy promotes stress-induced deformation twinning under dynamic tensile loading.
Reduced stacking-fault-energy regions facilitate coordinated activation of deformation twinning and dislocation slip.
Coordinated twinning and dislocation slip delay strain localization.
The coordinated twin-dislocation mechanism sustains high flow stress during dynamic tensile deformation.
Modified nanopillars are predicted to have significantly greater uniform elongation than homogeneous CoCrFeNi nanopillars.
The improvement in elongation is predicted to exceed 100% relative to the homogeneous baseline.
Modified specimens are predicted to retain flow stresses comparable to those of the homogeneous baseline.
Modified-composition regions are predicted to contain spatially distributed twin bands.
Modified-composition regions are predicted to contain well-developed dislocation arrays.
The proposed behavior is expected to hold for room-temperature tensile deformation of single-crystalline, <110>-oriented CoCrFeNi nanopillars.
After validation, the proposed behavior may extend to bulk materials of similar composition and processing history.
A controlled comparison will use modified and homogeneous CoCrFeNi specimens tested under identical room-temperature uniaxial tensile conditions.
Failure to observe both enhanced uniform elongation at maintained flow stress and coordinated twin bands and dislocation arrays relative to controls would falsify the hypothesis.
